Hernán Cortés.fact: The Licentiate then fell ill and died shortly after his arrival, appointing Marcos de Aguilar as alcalde mayor. In February 1527, the aged Aguilar fell ill in his turn and, before his death, appointed Alonso de Estrada to the position of governor, in which function he was confirmed by royal decree in August 1527.

Hernán Cortés.subject: Indian Languages
Hernán Cortés.question: In 1541, _____és returned to Spain, where he died six years later of natural causes
Hernán Cortés.fact: When the governor of Cuba sent emissaries to arrest Cortés, he fought them and won, using the extra troops as reinforcements. Cortés wrote letters directly to the king asking to be acknowledged for his successes instead of being punished for mutiny.

Hernán Cortés.subject: Indian Languages
Hernán Cortés.question: Until the _____th century, most writers continued to spell his first name as "Hernando" or the equivalent, "Fernando"
Hernán Cortés.fact: Until the 20th century, most writers continued to spell his first name as "Hernando" or the equivalent, "Fernando". However, in the 20th century, the conventional spelling has gradually shifted to the shortened form, "Hernán".

Hernán Cortés.subject: Indian Languages
Hernán Cortés.question: Upon his arrival in 1504 in _____, the capital of Hispaniola, the 18-year-old Cortés registered as a citizen; this entitled him to a building plot and land to farm
Hernán Cortés.fact: Upon his arrival in 1504 in Santo Domingo, the capital of Hispaniola, the 18-year-old Cortés registered as a citizen; this entitled him to a building plot and land to farm.

Hernán Cortés.subject: Indian Languages
Hernán Cortés.question: His next five years seemed to help establish him in the colony; in 1506, Cortés took part in the conquests of _____ and Cuba
Hernán Cortés.fact: Upon his arrival in 1504 in Santo Domingo, the capital of Hispaniola, the 18-year-old Cortés registered as a citizen; this entitled him to a building plot and land to farm. His next five years seemed to help establish him in the colony; in 1506, Cortés took part in the conquests of Hispaniola and Cuba.

Hernán Cortés.subject: Indian Languages
Hernán Cortés.question: He missed the first two expeditions, under the orders of _____ández de Córdoba and then Juan de Grijalva, sent by Diego Velázquez to Mexico in 1518
Hernán Cortés.fact: He missed the first two expeditions, under the orders of Francisco Hernández de Córdoba and then Juan de Grijalva, sent by Diego Velázquez to Mexico in 1518.

Hernán Cortés.subject: Indian Languages
Hernán Cortés.question: Cortés was appointed captain-general of this new expedition in _____ 1518, but was advised to move fast before Velázquez changed his mind
Hernán Cortés.fact: Cortés was appointed captain-general of this new expedition in October 1518, but was advised to move fast before Velázquez changed his mind.

Hernán Cortés.subject: Indian Languages
Hernán Cortés.question: In March 1519, Cortés formally claimed the land for the _____ crown
Hernán Cortés.fact: There he encountered Geronimo de Aguilar, a Spanish Franciscan priest who had survived a shipwreck followed by a period in captivity with the Maya, before escaping. In March 1519, Cortés formally claimed the land for the Spanish crown.

Hernán Cortés.subject: Indian Languages
Hernán Cortés.question: Leaving a hundred men in _____, Cortés marched on Tenochtitlán in mid-August 1519, along with 600 soldiers, 15 horsemen, 15 cannons, and hundreds of indigenous carriers and warriors
Hernán Cortés.fact: Leaving a hundred men in Veracruz, Cortés marched on Tenochtitlán in mid-August 1519, along with 600 soldiers, 15 horsemen, 15 cannons, and hundreds of indigenous carriers and warriors.

Hernán Cortés.subject: Indian Languages
Hernán Cortés.question: The Otomis and then the _____ clashed with the Spanish in a series of three battles from 2 to 5 September 1519, and at one point, Diaz remarked, "they surrounded us on every side"
Hernán Cortés.fact: The Otomis and then the Tlaxcalans clashed with the Spanish in a series of three battles from 2 to 5 September 1519, and at one point, Diaz remarked, "they surrounded us on every side".

Hernán Cortés.subject: Indian Languages
Hernán Cortés.question: In October 1519, Cortés and his men, accompanied by about 1,000 _____, marched to Cholula, the second-largest city in central Mexico
Hernán Cortés.fact: In October 1519, Cortés and his men, accompanied by about 1,000 Tlaxcalteca, marched to Cholula, the second-largest city in central Mexico.

Hernán Cortés.subject: Indian Languages
Hernán Cortés.question: On 8 _____ 1519, they were peacefully received by Moctezuma II
Hernán Cortés.fact: On 8 November 1519, they were peacefully received by Moctezuma II.

Hernán Cortés.subject: Indian Languages
Hernán Cortés.question: Meanwhile, Velázquez sent another expedition, led by Pánfilo de Narváez, to oppose Cortés, arriving in _____ in April 1520 with 1,100 men
Hernán Cortés.fact: Meanwhile, Velázquez sent another expedition, led by Pánfilo de Narváez, to oppose Cortés, arriving in Mexico in April 1520 with 1,100 men. In Mexico, one of Cortés's lieutenants Pedro de Alvarado, committed the massacre in the Great Temple, triggering a local rebellion.

Hernán Cortés.subject: Indian Languages
Hernán Cortés.question: In January 1521, Cortés countered a conspiracy against him, headed by _____ de Villafana, who was hanged for the offence
Hernán Cortés.fact: In January 1521, Cortés countered a conspiracy against him, headed by Antonio de Villafana, who was hanged for the offence.

Hernán Cortés.subject: Indian Languages
Hernán Cortés.question: From 1521 to 1524, Cortés personally governed _____
Hernán Cortés.fact: Finally, with the capture of Cuauhtémoc, the tlatoani (ruler) of Tenochtitlán, on 13 August 1521, the Mexica was conquered, and Cortés was able to claim it for Spain, thus renaming the city Mexico City. From 1521 to 1524, Cortés personally governed Mexico.

Hernán Cortés.subject: Indian Languages
Hernán Cortés.question: Cortés managed the founding of new cities and appointed men to extend Spanish rule to all of _____, imposing the encomienda system in 1524
Hernán Cortés.fact: King Charles appointed Cortés as governor, captain general and chief justice of the newly conquered territory, dubbed "New Spain of the Ocean Sea". Cortés managed the founding of new cities and appointed men to extend Spanish rule to all of New Spain, imposing the encomienda system in 1524.

Hernán Cortés.subject: Indian Languages
Hernán Cortés.question: In 1529, he had been accorded the noble designation of don, but more importantly, was given the noble title of _____ of the Valley of Oaxaca and married the Spanish noblewoman Doña Juana de Zúñiga
Hernán Cortés.fact: In 1529, he had been accorded the noble designation of don, but more importantly, was given the noble title of Marquess of the Valley of Oaxaca and married the Spanish noblewoman Doña Juana de Zúñiga. As the first-born legitimate son, Don Martín Cortés y Zúñiga was now Cortés's heir and succeeded him as holder of the title and estate of the Marquessate of the Valley of Oaxaca.

Hernán Cortés.subject: Indian Languages
Hernán Cortés.question: He therefore ordered _____ and Almíndez Chirino back to Mexico City to rejoin the government, which they did on 29 December 1524
Hernán Cortés.fact: The other two Gonzalo de Salazar and Pedro Almíndez Chirino (aka 'Peralmíndez'), accompanied him on campaign. He therefore ordered Salazar and Almíndez Chirino back to Mexico City to rejoin the government, which they did on 29 December 1524.

Hernán Cortés.subject: Indian Languages
Hernán Cortés.question: Indeed, he had spent lavishly to build the new capital of _____ on the ruins of the Aztec capital of Tenochtitlán, levelled during the siege that brought down the Aztec empire
Hernán Cortés.fact: Indeed, he had spent lavishly to build the new capital of Mexico City on the ruins of the Aztec capital of Tenochtitlán, levelled during the siege that brought down the Aztec empire.

Hernán Cortés.subject: Indian Languages
Hernán Cortés.question: He was received by _____ with every distinction and decorated with the order of Santiago
Hernán Cortés.fact: By this time, Charles had returned, and Cortés forthrightly responded to his enemy's charges. He was received by Charles with every distinction and decorated with the order of Santiago.

Hernán Cortés.subject: Indian Languages
Hernán Cortés.question: The noble title and senorial estate of the Marquesado were passed down to his descendants until _____
Hernán Cortés.fact: The noble title and senorial estate of the Marquesado were passed down to his descendants until 1811.

Hernán Cortés.subject: Indian Languages
Hernán Cortés.question: The Oaxaca Valley was one of the wealthiest regions of _____, and Cortés had 23,000 vassals in 23 named encomiendas in perpetuity
Hernán Cortés.fact: The Oaxaca Valley was one of the wealthiest regions of New Spain, and Cortés had 23,000 vassals in 23 named encomiendas in perpetuity. Although confirmed in his land holdings and vassals, he was not reinstated as governor and was never again given any important office in the administration of New Spain.

Hernán Cortés.subject: Indian Languages
Hernán Cortés.question: Although confirmed in his land holdings and vassals, he was not reinstated as governor and was never again given any important office in the administration of _____
Hernán Cortés.fact: The Oaxaca Valley was one of the wealthiest regions of New Spain, and Cortés had 23,000 vassals in 23 named encomiendas in perpetuity. Although confirmed in his land holdings and vassals, he was not reinstated as governor and was never again given any important office in the administration of New Spain.

Hernán Cortés.subject: Indian Languages
Hernán Cortés.question: During his travel to _____, his property was mismanaged by abusive colonial administrators
Hernán Cortés.fact: The Oaxaca Valley was one of the wealthiest regions of New Spain, and Cortés had 23,000 vassals in 23 named encomiendas in perpetuity. Although confirmed in his land holdings and vassals, he was not reinstated as governor and was never again given any important office in the administration of New Spain.

Hernán Cortés.subject: Indian Languages
Hernán Cortés.question: The natives documented the abuses in the _____
Hernán Cortés.fact: The natives documented the abuses in the Huexotzinco Codex.

Hernán Cortés.subject: Indian Languages
Hernán Cortés.question: The entailed estate and title passed to his legitimate son Don Martín Cortés upon Cortés's death in _____, who became the Second Marquess
Hernán Cortés.fact: The entailed estate and title passed to his legitimate son Don Martín Cortés upon Cortés's death in 1547, who became the Second Marquess.

Hernán Cortés.subject: Indian Languages
Hernán Cortés.question: Although Cortés still retained military authority and permission to continue his conquests, Don Antonio de Mendoza was appointed in _____ as a viceroy to administer New Spain's civil affairs
Hernán Cortés.fact: Although Cortés still retained military authority and permission to continue his conquests, Don Antonio de Mendoza was appointed in 1535 as a viceroy to administer New Spain's civil affairs.

Hernán Cortés.subject: Indian Languages
Hernán Cortés.question: This division of power led to continual dissension and caused the failure of several enterprises in which _____és was engaged
Hernán Cortés.fact: The entailed estate and title passed to his legitimate son Don Martín Cortés upon Cortés's death in 1547, who became the Second Marquess. Don Martín's association with the so-called Encomenderos' Conspiracy endangered the entailed holdings, but they were restored and remained the continuing reward for Hernán Cortés's family through the generations.

Hernán Cortés.subject: Indian Languages
Hernán Cortés.question: On returning to _____, Cortés found the country in a state of anarchy
Hernán Cortés.fact: On returning to Mexico, Cortés found the country in a state of anarchy. After reasserting his position and reestablishing some sort of order, Cortés retired to his estates at Cuernavaca, about 30 miles (48 km) south of Mexico City.

Hernán Cortés.subject: Indian Languages
Hernán Cortés.question: There was a strong suspicion in court circles of an intended rebellion by _____és
Hernán Cortés.fact: Although Cortés still retained military authority and permission to continue his conquests, Don Antonio de Mendoza was appointed in 1535 as a viceroy to administer New Spain's civil affairs. This division of power led to continual dissension and caused the failure of several enterprises in which Cortés was engaged.

Hernán Cortés.subject: Indian Languages
Hernán Cortés.question: After reasserting his position and reestablishing some sort of order, Cortés retired to his estates at Cuernavaca, about _____ (48 km) south of Mexico City
Hernán Cortés.fact: After reasserting his position and reestablishing some sort of order, Cortés retired to his estates at Cuernavaca, about 30 miles (48 km) south of Mexico City.

Hernán Cortés.subject: Indian Languages
Hernán Cortés.question: There, he concentrated on the building of his palace and on _____ exploration
Hernán Cortés.fact: There, he concentrated on the building of his palace and on Pacific exploration.

Hernán Cortés.subject: Indian Languages
Hernán Cortés.question: Remaining in Mexico between _____ and 1541, Cortés quarrelled with Nuño Beltrán de Guzmán and disputed the right to explore the territory that is today California with Antonio de Mendoza, the first vi
Hernán Cortés.fact: Remaining in Mexico between 1530 and 1541, Cortés quarrelled with Nuño Beltrán de Guzmán and disputed the right to explore the territory that is today California with Antonio de Mendoza, the first viceroy.

Hernán Cortés.subject: Indian Languages
Hernán Cortés.question: Cortés acquired several silver mines in Zumpango del Rio in _____
Hernán Cortés.fact: Cortés acquired several silver mines in Zumpango del Rio in 1534.

Hernán Cortés.subject: Indian Languages
Hernán Cortés.question: By the early 1540s, he owned 20 silver mines in _____, 12 in Taxco, and 3 in Zacualpan
Hernán Cortés.fact: By the early 1540s, he owned 20 silver mines in Sultepec, 12 in Taxco, and 3 in Zacualpan.

Hernán Cortés.subject: Indian Languages
Hernán Cortés.question: Earlier, Cortés had claimed the silver in the _____ area
Hernán Cortés.fact: Earlier, Cortés had claimed the silver in the Tamazula area.

Hernán Cortés.subject: Indian Languages
Hernán Cortés.question: In _____, Cortés explored the northwestern part of Mexico and discovered the Baja California peninsula
Hernán Cortés.fact: In 1536, Cortés explored the northwestern part of Mexico and discovered the Baja California peninsula.

Hernán Cortés.subject: Indian Languages
Hernán Cortés.question: Cortés also spent time exploring the _____ coast of Mexico
Hernán Cortés.fact: Cortés also spent time exploring the Pacific coast of Mexico.

Hernán Cortés.subject: Indian Languages
Hernán Cortés.question: The Gulf of California was originally named the Sea of Cortés by its discoverer Francisco de Ulloa in _____
Hernán Cortés.fact: The Gulf of California was originally named the Sea of Cortés by its discoverer Francisco de Ulloa in 1539.

Hernán Cortés.subject: Indian Languages
Hernán Cortés.question: This was the last major expedition by _____és
Hernán Cortés.fact: In 1536, Cortés explored the northwestern part of Mexico and discovered the Baja California peninsula. Cortés also spent time exploring the Pacific coast of Mexico.

Hernán Cortés.subject: Indian Languages
Hernán Cortés.question: During this campaign, Cortés was almost drowned in a storm that hit his fleet while he was pursuing the Pasha of _____
Hernán Cortés.fact: During this campaign, Cortés was almost drowned in a storm that hit his fleet while he was pursuing the Pasha of Algiers.

Hernán Cortés.subject: Indian Languages
Hernán Cortés.question: In February _____, he made a claim on the royal treasury, but was ignored for the next three years
Hernán Cortés.fact: In February 1544, he made a claim on the royal treasury, but was ignored for the next three years.

Hernán Cortés.subject: Indian Languages
Hernán Cortés.question: Disgusted, he decided to return to Mexico in _____
Hernán Cortés.fact: Disgusted, he decided to return to Mexico in 1547. He died in Castilleja de la Cuesta, Seville province, on 2 December 1547, from a case of pleurisy at the age of 62.

Hernán Cortés.subject: Indian Languages
Hernán Cortés.question: He died in Castilleja de la Cuesta, Seville province, on 2 December _____, from a case of pleurisy at the age of 62
Hernán Cortés.fact: Disgusted, he decided to return to Mexico in 1547. He died in Castilleja de la Cuesta, Seville province, on 2 December 1547, from a case of pleurisy at the age of 62.

Hernán Cortés.subject: Indian Languages
Hernán Cortés.question: When he reached _____, he was stricken with dysentery
Hernán Cortés.fact: When he reached Seville, he was stricken with dysentery. He died in Castilleja de la Cuesta, Seville province, on 2 December 1547, from a case of pleurisy at the age of 62.

Hernán Cortés.subject: Indian Languages
Hernán Cortés.question: He requested in his will that his remains eventually be buried in _____
Hernán Cortés.fact: He requested in his will that his remains eventually be buried in Mexico.

Hernán Cortés.subject: Indian Languages
Hernán Cortés.question: His daughter, Doña _____, however, died shortly after her father's death
Hernán Cortés.fact: His daughter, Doña Catalina, however, died shortly after her father's death.

Hernán Cortés.subject: Indian Languages
Hernán Cortés.question: On 4 December _____, he was buried in the mausoleum of the Duke of Medina in the church of San Isidoro del Campo, Sevilla
Hernán Cortés.fact: On 4 December 1547, he was buried in the mausoleum of the Duke of Medina in the church of San Isidoro del Campo, Sevilla.

Hernán Cortés.subject: Indian Languages
Hernán Cortés.question: In his testament, Cortés asked for his body to be buried in the monastery he had ordered to be built in _____ in México, ten years after his death, but the monastery was never built
Hernán Cortés.fact: In his testament, Cortés asked for his body to be buried in the monastery he had ordered to be built in Coyoacan in México, ten years after his death, but the monastery was never built.

Hernán Cortés.subject: Indian Languages
Hernán Cortés.question: So in _____, his body was sent to New Spain and buried in the church of San Francisco de Texcoco, where his mother and one of his sisters were buried
Hernán Cortés.fact: So in 1566, his body was sent to New Spain and buried in the church of San Francisco de Texcoco, where his mother and one of his sisters were buried.

Hernán Cortés.subject: Indian Languages
Hernán Cortés.question: In _____, Cortés's last male descendant, Don Pedro Cortés, fourth Marquez del Valle, died
Hernán Cortés.fact: In 1629, Cortés's last male descendant, Don Pedro Cortés, fourth Marquez del Valle, died.

Hernán Cortés.subject: Indian Languages
Hernán Cortés.question: The viceroy decided to move the bones of Cortés, along with those of his descendant, to the _____ church in México
Hernán Cortés.fact: The viceroy decided to move the bones of Cortés, along with those of his descendant, to the Franciscan church in México. Eventually, it was moved to the Sagrario of the Franciscan church, where it stayed for 87 years.

Hernán Cortés.subject: Indian Languages
Hernán Cortés.question: Eventually, it was moved to the _____ of the Franciscan church, where it stayed for 87 years
Hernán Cortés.fact: Eventually, it was moved to the Sagrario of the Franciscan church, where it stayed for 87 years.

Hernán Cortés.subject: Indian Languages
Hernán Cortés.question: In _____, it was moved to another place in the same church
Hernán Cortés.fact: In 1716, it was moved to another place in the same church.

Hernán Cortés.subject: Indian Languages
Hernán Cortés.question: In _____, his bones were moved to the "Hospital de Jesus" (founded by Cortés), where a statue by Tolsá and a mausoleum were made
Hernán Cortés.fact: In 1794, his bones were moved to the "Hospital de Jesus" (founded by Cortés), where a statue by Tolsá and a mausoleum were made.

Hernán Cortés.subject: Indian Languages
Hernán Cortés.question: In _____, after the independence of México, it seemed imminent that his body would be desecrated, so the mausoleum was removed, the statue and the coat of arms were sent to Palermo, Sicily, to be prot
Hernán Cortés.fact: In 1823, after the independence of México, it seemed imminent that his body would be desecrated, so the mausoleum was removed, the statue and the coat of arms were sent to Palermo, Sicily, to be protected by the Duke of Terranova.

Hernán Cortés.subject: Indian Languages
Hernán Cortés.question: In _____, his bones were moved to another place in the same building
Hernán Cortés.fact: In 1836, his bones were moved to another place in the same building.

Hernán Cortés.subject: Indian Languages
Hernán Cortés.question: It was not until 24 November _____, that they were rediscovered, thanks to the discovery of a secret document by Lucas Alamán
Hernán Cortés.fact: It was not until 24 November 1946, that they were rediscovered, thanks to the discovery of a secret document by Lucas Alamán.

Hernán Cortés.subject: Indian Languages
Hernán Cortés.question: His bones were put in the charge of the _____ de Antropología e Historia (INAH)
Hernán Cortés.fact: His bones were put in the charge of the Instituto Nacional de Antropología e Historia (INAH).

Hernán Cortés.subject: Indian Languages
Hernán Cortés.question: The remains were authenticated by _____
Hernán Cortés.fact: His bones were put in the charge of the Instituto Nacional de Antropología e Historia (INAH). The remains were authenticated by INAH.

Hernán Cortés.subject: Indian Languages
Hernán Cortés.question: Following the discovery and authentication of Cortés's remains, there was a discovery of what were described as the bones of _____émoc, resulting in a "battle of the bones"
Hernán Cortés.fact: When the bones were first rediscovered, the supporters of the Hispanic tradition in Mexico were excited, but one supporter of an indigenist vision of Mexico "proposed that the remains be publicly burned in front of the statue of Cuauhtemoc, and the ashes flung into the air". Following the discovery and authentication of Cortés's remains, there was a discovery of what were described as the bones of Cuauhtémoc, resulting in a "battle of the bones".

Hernán Cortés.subject: Indian Languages
Hernán Cortés.question: On 16 December _____, the lawsuits related to vassals of the Cortes estate were resolved by a royal order issued by Philip II
Hernán Cortés.fact: On 16 December 1560, the lawsuits related to vassals of the Cortes estate were resolved by a royal order issued by Philip II.

Hernán Cortés.subject: Indian Languages
Hernán Cortés.question: Another main source is the biography written by _____és's private chaplain Lopez de Gómara, which was written in Spain several years after the conquest
Hernán Cortés.fact: Following the discovery and authentication of Cortés's remains, there was a discovery of what were described as the bones of Cuauhtémoc, resulting in a "battle of the bones". On 16 December 1560, the lawsuits related to vassals of the Cortes estate were resolved by a royal order issued by Philip II.

Hernán Cortés.subject: Indian Languages
Hernán Cortés.question: Gómara never set foot in the _____ and knew only what Cortés had told him, and he had an affinity for knightly romantic stories, which he incorporated richly in the biography
Hernán Cortés.fact: Gómara never set foot in the Americas and knew only what Cortés had told him, and he had an affinity for knightly romantic stories, which he incorporated richly in the biography.

Hernán Cortés.subject: Indian Languages
Hernán Cortés.question: In the years following the conquest, more critical accounts of the _____ arrival in Mexico were written
Hernán Cortés.fact: In the years following the conquest, more critical accounts of the Spanish arrival in Mexico were written.

Hernán Cortés.subject: Indian Languages
Hernán Cortés.question: The accounts of the conquest given in the _____ by the Franciscan Bernardino de Sahagún and his native informants are also less than flattering towards Cortés
Hernán Cortés.fact: The accounts of the conquest given in the Florentine Codex by the Franciscan Bernardino de Sahagún and his native informants are also less than flattering towards Cortés.

Hernán Cortés.subject: Indian Languages
Hernán Cortés.question: However, many landmarks still bear his name, from the castle _____ de Cortés in the city of Cuernavaca to some street names throughout the republic
Hernán Cortés.fact: However, many landmarks still bear his name, from the castle Palacio de Cortés in the city of Cuernavaca to some street names throughout the republic.

Hernán Cortés.subject: Indian Languages
Hernán Cortés.question: The pass between the volcanoes Iztaccíhuatl and _____épetl, where Cortés took his soldiers on their march to Mexico City, is known as the Paso de Cortés
Hernán Cortés.fact: The pass between the volcanoes Iztaccíhuatl and Popocatépetl, where Cortés took his soldiers on their march to Mexico City, is called the Paso de Cortés.

Hernán Cortés.subject: Indian Languages
Hernán Cortés.question: The muralist _____ painted several representations of him, but the most famous one depicts him as a powerful and ominous figure along with Malinche in a mural in the National Palace in Mexico City
Hernán Cortés.fact: The muralist Diego Rivera painted several representations of him, but the most famous one depicts him as a powerful and ominous figure along with Malinche in a mural in the National Palace in Mexico City.

Hernán Cortés.subject: Indian Languages
Hernán Cortés.question: In _____, President Lopez Portillo tried to bring Cortés to public recognition
Hernán Cortés.fact: In 1981, President Lopez Portillo tried to bring Cortés to public recognition.

Hernán Cortés.subject: Indian Languages
Hernán Cortés.question: Today the copy of the bust is in the "_____ de Jesús Nazareno" while the original is in Naples, Italy, in the Villa Pignatelli
Hernán Cortés.fact: First, he made public a copy of the bust of Cortés made by Manuel Tolsá in the Hospital de Jesús Nazareno with an official ceremony, but soon a nationalist group tried to destroy it, so it had to be taken out of the public. Today the copy of the bust is in the "Hospital de Jesús Nazareno" while the original is in Naples, Italy, in the Villa Pignatelli.

Hernán Cortés.subject: Indian Languages
Hernán Cortés.question: The statue depicts Cortés, _____ and their son Martín
Hernán Cortés.fact: The statue depicts Cortés, Malinche and their son Martín.

Hernán Cortés.subject: Indian Languages
Hernán Cortés.question: There is another statue by _____án Aparicio, in Cuernavaca, which was in a hotel "El casino de la selva"
Hernán Cortés.fact: There is another statue by Sebastián Aparicio, in Cuernavaca, which was in a hotel "El casino de la selva".

Hernán Cortés.subject: Indian Languages
Hernán Cortés.question: The hotel was closed to make a commercial centre, and the statue was put out of public display by _____, the builder of the commercial centre
Hernán Cortés.fact: The hotel was closed to make a commercial centre, and the statue was put out of public display by Costco, the builder of the commercial centre.

Hernán Cortés.subject: Indian Languages
Hernán Cortés.question: His first letter was considered lost, and the one from the municipality of _____ has to take its place
Hernán Cortés.fact: His first letter was considered lost, and the one from the municipality of Veracruz has to take its place.

Hernán Cortés.subject: Indian Languages
Hernán Cortés.question: It was published for the first time in volume IV of "_____ para la Historia de España", and subsequently reprinted
Hernán Cortés.fact: It was published for the first time in volume IV of "Documentos para la Historia de España", and subsequently reprinted.

Hernán Cortés.subject: Indian Languages
Hernán Cortés.question: The Segunda Carta de Relacion, bearing the date of 30 October _____, appeared in print at Seville in 1522
Hernán Cortés.fact: The Segunda Carta de Relacion, bearing the date of 30 October 1520, appeared in print at Seville in 1522.

Hernán Cortés.subject: Indian Languages
Hernán Cortés.question: The third letter, dated 15 May _____, appeared at Seville in 1523
Hernán Cortés.fact: The Segunda Carta de Relacion, bearing the date of 30 October 1520, appeared in print at Seville in 1522. The third letter, dated 15 May 1522, appeared at Seville in 1523.

Hernán Cortés.subject: Indian Languages
Hernán Cortés.question: The fourth, 20 October _____, was printed at Toledo in 1525
Hernán Cortés.fact: The fourth, 20 October 1524, was printed at Toledo in 1525.

Hernán Cortés.subject: Indian Languages
Hernán Cortés.question: The fifth, on the _____ expedition, is contained in volume IV of the Documentos para la Historia de España
Hernán Cortés.fact: The fifth, on the Honduras expedition, is contained in volume IV of the Documentos para la Historia de España.

Hernán Cortés.subject: Indian Languages
Hernán Cortés.question: Doña _____ married Juan de Salcedo, a conqueror and encomendero, with whom she had a son, Pedro
Hernán Cortés.fact: Doña Catalina married Juan de Salcedo, a conqueror and encomendero, with whom she had a son, Pedro.
